sites.meaning: Reject PPID->channel table values with bit 9 set (channel >= 0x200) before the arbiter is touched. The vendor check at 0x3584 only rejects bit 10 (>= 0x400); the two tests together reject every value >= 0x200. The reject path returns 0x1c (unsupported) at 0x35dc, so the caller aborts the transaction at 0x294c without reading the arbiter.
sites.evidence: FAR 0x000000000C777008 in v16 (and 0x0C77A008 in v10) = arbiter base 0x0C500008 + channel 0x277/0x27A << 12, read by 0x37F0. The channel comes from the runtime PPID->channel lookup at 0x3578, which never range-checks the table value (0x3668 loads ctx[68], 0x372c adds the looked-up value, 0x3734 masks to 0xffff, 0x373c shifts by 12). The vendor rejects bit 10 but not bit 9, so 0x277 is accepted and the unimplemented channel aborts.

meaning: Restore the stock SPMI driver completely (entry point and channel execute routine are stock again) and reject arbiter channels >= 0x200 at the PPID->channel lookup, so the PMIC/SPMI path works for the provisioned channels while an unprogrammed table entry returns EFI_UNSUPPORTED instead of an external abort.
evidence: v17 stubbed the DXE entry (no SPMI protocol, PmicDxe Locate protocol failed, ASSERT pm_comm_spmi_lite.c +66). v18 stubbed the whole channel execute routine at RVA 0x3668 (no abort, but every transfer a silent no-op, and the PMIC PON path the volume/power keys need stayed dead). v19 keeps both stock and only adds the range check.
limitations: Any SPMI channel index of 0x200 or above is rejected by the protocol lookup: an unsupported or unprogrammed PPID now returns EFI_UNSUPPORTED (28) instead of issuing the arbiter read that aborted the AP. Every provisioned PMIC channel is below 0x100, so those transfers keep their stock behaviour and the PMIC/PON path stays alive. If a future slave legitimately needs a channel above 0x1FF the guard must be replaced by a range check against the per-EE channel count in the context record at ctx+48.
